loops.operand_stats: Triple-nested naive GEMM over single-precision float (32-bit IEEE-754) elements stored row-major in a fixed float[100] array (MAX_ELEMENTS) inside a struct with unsigned char (8-bit) rows/columns. Innermost body is a float multiply-accumulate: C[i][j] += A[i][k] * B[k][j]. getElement/setElement are inlined (no separate call counts in the profile; all cycles land in multiply). Each inner iteration recomputes three 1-based indices (row-1)*columns+(column-1) -> an 8-bit*8-bit integer multiply-add per access, then a 4-byte scaled address. Memory pattern: A walked unit-stride along k (row), B walked with stride = B.columns*4 bytes along k (column), C[i][j] loaded and stored every k iteration (loop-carried accumulator recurrence through memory, since matrixC aliasing with A/B is not excluded). Candidate patterns: fused float MAC (fmadd.s), fused 2D index computation (idx = (r-1)*cols+(c-1) with base+scale), strided load, keeping the C accumulator in a register. Dimensions bounded by 100 elements, so k trip count <= 100 per (i,j). Exact trip count unknown from sources (harness-driven).

Inlined clearMatrix inside multiply: fixed 100-iteration unit-stride store of 32-bit float zero to C.elements; no loads, no recurrence. Negligible share relative to the MAC nest; included only for completeness of multiply's cycles.
